sections.body: Artificial intelligence in accounting and finance is mostly applied to document heavy, repetitive, and pattern rich work. Systems read invoices, contracts, receipts, and statements, then extract fields, match them to ledgers, and flag exceptions for a person to review. Forecasting models combine historical results with external signals to produce rolling budgets, cash projections, and scenario plans. Tax tools map transactions to rules across jurisdictions and prepare workpapers, while audit tools sample populations continuously instead of once a year. Fraud models score transactions for unusual patterns, and treasury models estimate liquidity needs. The field is not a single product but a set of narrow tools that sit inside existing accounting workflows.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Much of the routine work is now automated well, including invoice capture, three way matching, bank reconciliation, expense coding, and basic anomaly detection at scale in many finance departments. Forecasting has improved for stable businesses, but it still struggles with structural breaks, new products, and sudden market shifts. Tax and audit remain harder because rules change, evidence must be defensible, and a wrong answer can carry penalties. Fraud detection produces alerts, not proof, and investigators still need to establish intent and build a case. Sustainability accounting lacks consistent measurement for many emissions sources, and digital asset accounting faces valuation, custody, and classification questions. Governance is the least settled area, and the site's 215 compliance and regulation pages show how much of the work is shaped by external rules rather than by the models alone.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Financial Reporting and Synthesis covers the close, consolidation, and narrative generation that turn ledger data into statements. Forecasting and Planning follows the budget cycle, driver based models, and scenario analysis used by finance teams. Tax and Jurisdictional Compliance deals with multi country rules, indirect taxes, and transfer pricing documentation. Continuous Audit and Assurance and Fraud Detection and Forensics sit on the control side, one for ongoing evidence and one for investigation and loss recovery. Payables and Receivables and Treasury and Liquidity cover the cash engine, from supplier invoices and customer collections to bank balances and funding needs. Sustainability and Carbon Accounting and Digital Asset Accounting handle newer asset and disclosure classes, while Governance, Risk and Financial Data Security ties model oversight, access controls, and data protection together.
